A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same selective-inference approach to kNN anomaly detection, despite substantial revision and retitling. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments, evaluations on ten tabular datasets and ten MVTec classes, ablations, and image case studies.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and real-data experiments, including heterogeneous-signal simulations and non-Gaussian robustness results.

M1.justification: V1 tests against the average signal of k neighbors using an L1 statistic, with a separate mean-based image statistic. V2 instead tests against the kth neighbor alone and specifies an L2 statistic, projection/direction conditioning, and chi-based p-values. These substantially change the inferential procedure.

E1.justification: The ten tabular datasets and ten MVTec classes are retained. V2 adds heterogeneous synthetic signals with differing means and tests departures from Gaussian noise using exponentially modified Gaussian, generalized normal, skew normal, and Student's t distributions. These introduce materially different input-distribution scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds Hotelling_t2 to synthetic comparisons and the tabular/image Type I error comparisons in Figure 4. V1 compared only naive, Bonferroni, w/o-pp, and image-specific OpA1/OpA2. V2 also changes the documented naive comparator from a classical z-test to a chi-based test.

E3.justification: Main synthetic experiments change d from 2 to 5 and replace the stated mean-shift procedure with shifts in one randomly selected coordinate. Appendix dimension sweeps and default k change. Fixed-k tabular comparisons are removed, and the reported image setting changes from k=1 to k=3. New robustness experiments vary Wasserstein distance and test significance levels 0.05 and 0.1.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit tests of robustness to four non-Gaussian distributions in Appendix C.2/Figure 10. Existing n/d/k sensitivity analyses are revised and extended across parametric and heterogeneous-signal settings. The principal ablation roles remain, while image case studies expand from one to two anomalous examples per class.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 synthetic trials per configuration and display error bars for real-data results. Neither defines those bars or provides seeds, and v2 introduces no new experimental uncertainty-estimation procedure. Additional result curves retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Synthetic curves are replaced under revised settings, and new baseline, robustness, and image-example results are reported. V2 Figure 3 shows Hotelling_t2 exceeding the proposed method at smaller parametric signal strengths, while Figure 2 shows its failure to control errors under heterogeneous signals. Many real-data power bars are retained; the changed methods and settings preclude interpreting the revision as a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 restricts general noise covariance to σ²I and replaces v1's sign-conditioned, truncated-normal derivation with new nuisance conditioning and chi-distribution Theorems 4.1–4.2 and proofs. The revision contains substantive inconsistencies: Eqs. (10)–(11) do not reproduce Eq. (6), the stated chi degrees of freedom are unsupported, and Appendix B.3 retains a truncated-Gaussian computation.

C1.justification: The central claim remains selective-inference significance testing with false-positive control for kNN, including learned features. V2 more explicitly frames the contribution as a proof-of-concept test for an existing deep-kNN detector and distinguishes uncertainty quantification from developing a detector with improved accuracy.

C2.justification: V2 replaces v1's linear-statistic-only limitation with a specific limitation concerning Transformers and complex selection events, extends stated distance applicability to L∞, and interprets the new robustness results as supporting approximate control under small noise departures. The Gaussian-noise caveat remains.

D1.justification: V2 newly announces and links an open-source implementation and experimental scripts, providing substantial reproducibility access information absent from v1. It also specifies the AMD EPYC 9474F processor, 48-core CPU, and 768 GB memory. Existing ResNet, patch-extraction, standardization, and dataset-source descriptions are largely retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands related work into parametric, classical machine-learning, and deep-learning AD categories, adding references on Deep SVDD, GAN/VAE/diffusion methods, and further SI developments. It more specifically positions the contribution against deep-kNN detection and distinguishes individual-anomaly testing from regression after outlier removal and global change-point testing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, problem setup, and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work moves into the introduction, much of v1 Section 4 moves into Appendix B, and scope, limitations, and conclusions are combined. The title and method terminology also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts compact conference formatting, removes v1's pipeline schematic, introduces a prominent Capsule example and synthetic-data illustrations, and combines real-data plots into Figure 4. Synthetic panels are reorganized around parametric/semi-parametric settings, while redesigned image-example panels are divided between the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 improves experimental coverage, comparison breadth, presentation, and reproducibility information. However, v1's linear-statistic/truncated-normal derivation is replaced by incompatible formulas: v2's scalar contrast in Eqs. (10)–(11) is not Eq. (6)'s L2 statistic, Theorem 4.1 assigns an unsupported (1+n)d-degree chi law, and Appendix B.3 still prescribes a truncated Gaussian. These defects undermine the stated derivation and computation of the central false-positive guarantee, outweighing the added experiments.
